gates.claim: curveDx and curveDy as declared in FiveTwoCurveDeriv.lean really are the partials of the curve -- central differences at step 1e-20 agree

curveDy(x, y_j) is the cubic's derivative at its own root, so it vanishes exactly when that root is multiple -- the product over the three roots is the discriminant up to the leading coefficient, and is nonzero off the locus

THE IFT HYPOTHESIS ON THE ARC. min_j |curveDy| >= 1.6158 everywhere on |x| = 1 away from the branch point, and VANISHES at phi_0. phi_0 is SOLVED FOR, not sampled: the lane's proved characterisation gives Q(2 cos phi_0) = 0 with Q(u) = u^4-6u^3+7u^2+6u-31, so phi_0/pi = 0.76622594937757503001 and min |curveDy| there is 1.8e-25 -- the square-root accuracy floor for a DOUBLE root at 50 dps, which is what it is. So exists_hasDerivAt_root applies on [0,pi] minus {phi_0} and fails nowhere else, matching exists_unit_circle_disc_zero exactly. (An earlier draft of this gate quoted a refinement sequence that went 0.0177 -> 0.0249: it was BRACKETING phi_0, not converging to it. Quoting a grid value as a minimum is the defect this lane already found once, in min|disc| = 0.348.)

the IFT VALUE is right: dy/dphi from finite differences on a tracked root matches -(curveDx/curveDy) * dx/dphi. The envelope does not need this value -- only that the derivative exists -- but a wrong value would mean a wrong partial, so it is checked
at the base point x = 1 all three roots are simple -- |curveDy| bounded away from zero for each -- so the IFT applies where the transport starts

THE ENVELOPE COLLAPSE, checked directly. d/dphi V(x, y(phi)) equals (partial V/partial x)*dx/dphi -- the dy/dphi term drops out because partial V/partial y = 0 on the curve, which deformed_saddle_iff_curve makes free. This is the identity the whole IFT brick exists to license

verdict.hypothesis_holds_where_it_must: min_j |curveDy| along the arc is bounded away from zero except at phi_0/pi ~ 0.7662, where refinement drives it to zero -- exactly the branch point exists_unit_circle_disc_zero proves. So the IFT covers [0,pi] minus one point.
verdict.envelope_collapse_verified: G6: d/dphi V(x, y(phi)) = (partial V/partial x) * dx/dphi to better than 1e-10 by finite differences. The dy/dphi term drops because partial V/partial y = 0 on the curve.
verdict.what_remains: assembling the collapse over the three roots in Lean, the Vieta sum giving sum_j partial V/partial x = -2 log x / x, and gluing across phi_0 with ConstantOffOnePoint. None of that is written.
